# 2 Baruch Chapter 10 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** The Fall of Jerusalem

---

**1** "Better never to have been born, or — having been born — to have died young.

**2** But we who are alive — how terrible for us! We have to watch Zion suffer and see what has happened to Jerusalem.

**3** I call on the sirens of the sea, on the night-spirits of the desert, on the demons and jackals of the forests: Wake up! Gird yourselves for grieving and join me in mourning!

**4** Zion, do not weep for me — weep for yourself! Weep for the desolation left by your Comforter who once was near you.

**5** The righteous have been swept away. The prophets have fallen silent. We have been driven from our land. Zion herself has been taken from us. We have nothing left now but the Mighty One and his Law.

**6** If we strip out all the vanity from our hearts and turn back to the Mighty One, he will restore everything we have lost — and multiply it many times over.

**7** As for the righteous of this age — righteousness itself is their reward. They will rejoice and not be put to shame.

**8** Those whose fathers were taught wisdom will receive what they are owed. Those trained by wise leaders will not be displaced.

**9** But here we are, still carrying a name we inherited from our ancestors, while we ourselves have become strangers to what that name means.

**10** What can we even say to those settled in Babylon? What can we say to the ones scattered there?

**11** Zion is gone. We have no refuge.

**12** We abandoned our homeland. We have no inheritance anywhere else either.

**13** Brides, do not go into your wedding chambers. Virgins, stop weaving your garlands. Wives, stop praying for children.

**14** Pregnant women, do not pray for safe delivery. The childless will find it easier. Those with no sons are the lucky ones. Those who have sons will grieve.

**15** Why beget children only to hand them over to the grave?

**16** Why should humanity keep going if it is only headed for destruction?

**17** Why should a man build a household if it will only be stripped from him?

**18** Why endure the pain of childbirth if the child will be cut down before maturity?

**19** Why dress in the splendor of youth, why adorn yourself with beauty, if it is all destined to sink into the grave?"

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic rendering. V.1 echoes Job 3 and Jer 20. V.3 the mythological mourners rendered for vividness. Vv.11-12 as short statements for rhetorical punch. Vv.15-19 rendered as pointed questions without the repetitive "Or why should...?" formula.*
